clue.text: Joint in bricks flamboyant? Not half!

indicators.note: not half means only one half of the word survives, the front five of its ten letters

blocks.note: Lego is the brand of toy building bricks
the first half of the ten-letter word

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a roast built out of toy bricks is flamboyant, and gets a firm reply.
explanation.walkthrough: LEGO + FLAMB, re-spaced, reads LEG OF LAMB.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg of lamb is a classic roasting cut, and a joint is a large cut of meat for roasting.

blocks.note: first meaning: to not take it
second meaning: a holiday from work

explanation.surface: Advice not to have a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface runs the two meanings together as one instruction; split it after 'take'.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means abandon or not pick up; the noun means permitted absence from work.

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by speech, so it is the sound that counts here

blocks.note: a bargain is a good buy

explanation.surface: A cheap deal is said to have lasted ages.
explanation.definitionFit: 'So long' is an informal farewell, the same parting phrase.

blocks.note: to fell is to knock down, as with a tree or a boxer
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone flattens a man they are only loosely seeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casual' looks like it describes the relationship, but it marks the informal spelling of 'fellow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fella is slang for a man, and especially for a boyfriend, as in 'her fella'.

clue.text: Fruit found in bed after almost thirty days

indicators.note: almost means falling just short, so the final letter is lost

blocks.note: April has thirty days; its last letter goes
a cot is a small bed; 'after' puts it at the end

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit is discovered in a bed nearly a month later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thirty days' points to one of the months with thirty days; April is the one that fits.
explanation.definitionFit: The apricot is a small orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Game bird is all gone to pot

indicators.note: something gone to pot has fallen into disorder, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Game birds have all ended up in the cooking pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game bird' reads as one phrase, but 'Game' alone is the definition; 'pot' also hints at potting balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Billiards is a cue game played on a cloth-covered table with balls and pockets.

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter of the word before it is kept

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
the leading letter of age
Orlando is this puzzle's setter, so the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: Someone nominates the setter as the head of the New Age movement.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's own pseudonym in the clue stands for ME, the setter speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: To call someone something is to name them, as in calling a child Tom.

clue.text: Short book's length restricted by star

indicators.note: something restricted is hemmed in on both sides by what follows

blocks.note: a nova is a star that suddenly brightens
an ell is an old measure of cloth length

explanation.surface: A brief novel is only as long as its famous author allows.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay. ELL is an old English unit, about 45 inches.
explanation.definitionFit: A novella is a work of fiction longer than a short story but shorter than a novel.

clue.text: Gender of Uncle Sam, I recollected

indicators.note: re-collected means gathered up again, so these letters are reassembled in a fresh order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone remembers what sex the American national figure was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' reads as remembered; split it as re-collected.
explanation.definitionFit: Masculine is one of the grammatical genders, alongside feminine and neuter.

blocks.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
taken as written
a roller is a long heavy sea wave

explanation.surface: A vocalist is swept up by the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A caroller is someone who sings carols, typically going door to door at Christmas.

clue.text: Sumptuous little room is first in house

indicators.note: first in points to the opening letter of the following word only

blocks.note: lav, short for lavatory, is a small room
taken as written
the opening letter of house

explanation.surface: A luxurious small room is the main feature of a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little room' is the British euphemism for a toilet; lav is short for lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish and sumptuous both describe something rich, splendid and expensive.

clue.text: Dancing bear is somewhere in the Balkans

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and land in a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A performing bear turns up in south-eastern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Serbia is a country on the Balkan peninsula, with Belgrade as its capital.

clue.text: Kid almost gets yob to relax

indicators.note: almost means falling just short, so the final letter is lost

blocks.note: a kid is a child; drop its last letter
a yob, British slang for a hooligan, is a lout

explanation.surface: A youngster nearly persuades a thug to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: A yob is a British word for a rowdy, aggressive young man.
explanation.definitionFit: To chill out is slang for unwinding and calming down.

indicators.note: about means going around, so the first word wraps the second

blocks.note: an alert is a warning
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone cautions about Edward the Black Prince, the medieval English heir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black Prince' looks like one historical title; split it, with Black the letter and Prince the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Albert was Queen Victoria's consort, a well-known royal prince.

clue.text: Fancy a drink of whisky straight away?

blocks.note: to fancy something is to like it
taken as written
a shot is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: An offer of a whisky to be drunk immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Like a shot is an idiom for instantly, without hesitation, as fast as a bullet.

clue.text: Cast seen twice after theatre's opening in state

indicators.note: an opening is the very start, so only the first letter of the word is kept
cast means thrown about, so these letters land in a new order

blocks.note: the opening letter of theatre
two copies of seen, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A theatre company is spotted twice on opening night somewhere in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the theatre's actors, but it signals scrambling; 'twice' doubles the fodder word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee is one of the fifty US states, home of Nashville and Memphis.

indicators.note: trained means shaped and drilled into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A tradesman teaches a water-dwelling animal its tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle.

blocks.note: to skip something is to omit it
worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: An instruction to omit the labourers' legwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workers'' seems to own the trousers, but it stands for insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski pants are close-fitting trousers worn for skiing.

clue.text: Slow and laborious worker — PC before red revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: Plod is British slang for the police, after Mr Plod the policeman in Noddy
the colour word, to be turned around

explanation.surface: A dull worker with a police constable heading a communist uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: PC is a British police constable; 'red revolution' suggests communism but asks for a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plodder works steadily and slowly, without flair.

blocks.note: as and since both mean because
RE is the British school subject Religious Education

explanation.surface: Someone untouched, like a religion lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaffected here means genuine and without pretence, which is what sincere means.

clue.text: Family member in Barts is terrific

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters running across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A relative working at Barts is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: Barts is St Bartholomew's, a London hospital, where a sister is also a senior nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: A sister is a female sibling, a member of the family.

blocks.note: to spar is to box in practice
tan is a light yellowish-brown

explanation.surface: A Greek container coloured pale brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' reads as a noun, a container; it is the verb, to fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spartan was a citizen of Sparta, an ancient Greek city-state.

indicators.note: turning letters are churned about into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A ruler going white with fear protests desperately.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of the French in 1804.

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
lamas are Tibetan Buddhist monks

explanation.surface: Livestock abandoned in the care of a monastery.
explanation.walkthrough: The animal and the monk differ by one L, which the clue supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Llamas are South American camelid pack animals.

indicators.note: missing means something is absent, so the following item is taken out

blocks.note: to launch is to start
the letter to take out

explanation.surface: Someone begins by skipping a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is the letter removed, not an article for meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunch is the midday meal.

indicators.note: from says the letters are drawn out of the words that follow

blocks.note: letters across the gap between the words

explanation.surface: A message received from a broadcasting celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: The number points to 2 Down, whose answer is a farewell; this is the Spanish version.
explanation.definitionFit: Adios is Spanish for farewell, an equivalent of the answer at 2 Down.

clue.text: Sunglasses in lavender, lilac, magnolia etc

blocks.note: first meaning: informal word for dark glasses
second meaning: these are pale colours, varieties of tint

explanation.surface: Dark glasses available in a range of pastel frames.
explanation.walkthrough: The three words look like flowers but are colour names, as on a paint chart.
explanation.definitionFit: Shades is slang for sunglasses, and colour variants are called shades.

indicators.note: naughty letters misbehave and refuse to stay in their order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A scientist from the Naughty Nineties, the racy 1890s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty Nineties' is a set phrase for the 1890s, which hides the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein was the physicist behind the theory of relativity.

blocks.note: first meaning: to move slightly
second meaning: slang for prison

explanation.walkthrough: Jug looks like a pouring vessel, suggesting mixing; here it is British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir means to budge or rouse, and is old slang for gaol, like jug.

clue.text: They never forget footballer returning to county

indicators.note: returning means coming back the way it went, so the name is read backwards

blocks.note: Pelé was the great Brazilian footballer
Hants is the abbreviation for Hampshire, an English county

explanation.surface: Fans recall a star player coming back to his home county.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying goes that an elephant never forgets, so these animals are the ones with long memories.
